title: Confidence-Bounded Unit-Test Rewards for Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards

contributions.purpose: Addresses the noisy pass-rate reward in RLVR for code generation when only a small number m of unit tests can be executed per rollout.
contributions.mechanism: The Lower Confidence Bound (LCB) reward models test outcomes as Bernoulli trials with a Beta prior and uses the delta-quantile of the Beta posterior over the true pass probability as a conservative reward penalizing high-uncertainty solutions.
contributions.evaluation: Trained with GRPO and evaluated on MBPP+ and HumanEval+ against pass-rate and other reward baselines.
contributions.source_quote: We propose the LCB reward for unit-test RLVR, which uses the lower confidence bound of a Beta posterior to account for finite-sample uncertainty in pass-rate estimation.

contributions.purpose: Shows the LCB reward improves accuracy while halving verifier compute compared to simply running more tests.
contributions.mechanism: Empirical comparison of LCB with m=5 tests against Pass-rate with 2m=10 tests and other baselines on code benchmarks.
contributions.evaluation: LCB (m=5) achieves best Pass@1 on MBPP+ (57.0%) and HumanEval+ (57.1%), outperforming Pass-rate (2m=10) while using only half the verifier compute.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that LCB (m=5) achieves state-of-the-art Pass@1 accuracy on MBPP+ (57.0%) and HumanEval+ (57.1%), outperforming Pass-rate (2m=10) while using only half the verifier compute.

contributions.purpose: Establishes the practical reliability of the LCB reward for training.
contributions.mechanism: Sensitivity analysis over hyperparameters (delta, prior) and comparison of training dynamics across all tested reward functions.
contributions.evaluation: LCB is robust to hyperparameter choices (delta, prior) and exhibits the most stable training dynamics among all tested reward functions.
contributions.source_quote: We show that LCB is robust to hyperparameter choices (delta, prior) and exhibits the most stable training dynamics among all tested reward functions.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work applies a similar conservative principle to unit-test rewards, as detailed in Section 3.4.
These approaches focus on learned reward models, whereas our method addresses the inherent statistical uncertainty in verifiable unit-test rewards.
Our approach is complementary: rather than improving test quality or increasing test count, we provide a principled way to account for uncertainty given a fixed number of tests.

notes: Positions itself as transferring the pessimism-under-uncertainty principle (Conservative Q-Learning, pessimistic reward models) to unit-test RLVR rewards. Machine-generation warning with code at gitlab.com/fars-a/confidence-bounded-unit-test-rewards.
